correctness.rationale: Sign counts on exactly 24 FCC-cell edges yield six or eight section sides according as three absolute normal coordinates satisfy triangle inequalities. The cubic section-face test has six or four sides for the same alternatives, giving pointwise complementarity. The triangle-inequality cone has explicit rays and solid angle 2 atan(sqrt(2)/5); dividing by the octant angle pi/2 proves the exact probability. Degenerate orientations have surface measure zero. A standalone program reconstructs all edges and checks the equality on sampled normals; it is not treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result completes a canonical discrete stereological observable of the perfect FCC Voronoi cell and proves a surprising directionwise relation to the simple-cubic cell, rather than recomputing a random arbitrary polyhedron. Both are fundamental crystallographic space-fillers. It gives a complete two-type law and an exact transfer of a known cube probability to a distinct geometric structure via an explicit sign-incidence theorem; this has a plausible use interpreting ideal crystalline planar microsections. It does not purport to be a general theorem for all solids.
